title: Separable Rank of Radial Kernels in Two and Higher Dimensions: Machine-Checked Proofs in Lean 4 and Isabelle/HOL
abstract: A d-variate kernel K : X_0 x ... x X_{d-1} -> K over a commutative semiring K has separable rank srank_K(K) in N u {infinity} equal to the least integer R in N for which K(x) = sum_{n=0}^{R-1} prod_{j=0}^{d-1} f_{n,j}(x_j) (or infinity if no finite R exists). On a d-dimensional Cartesian grid of stencil width W, a rank-R kernel evaluates in d R W one-dimensional taps per grid point rather than W^d. While a positive Gaussian exp(-alpha ||x||^2) has separable rank 1, approximating flat-top or oscillatory isotropic kernels---such as defocus disks, Airy point-spread functions, circular low-pass filters, or low-dispersion wave propagators---with finite coordinatewise rank relies on signed profiles built from complex-rate Gaussians and exponential polynomials. We present a complete machine-checked characterization in Lean 4 (with Mathlib) of the d-way separable rank of continuous circularly and spherically symmetric kernels K(x) = phi(||x||^2) on R^d for all d >= 2: (1) srank_R(K) < infinity if and only if the real profile phi agrees on [0, infinity) with a canonical exponential-polynomial representation R = {(lambda_u, P_u)}_{u=1}^m, phi(s) = sum_{u=1}^m Re(P_u(s) exp(lambda_u s)), with nonzero polynomials P_u in C[X], distinct rates lambda_u satisfying Im(lambda_u) >= 0, and P_u in R[X] whenever Im(lambda_u) = 0; (2) over C, a continuous profile psi on [0, infinity) satisfies srank_C(x |-> psi(||x||^2)) = R if and only if psi(s) = sum_{mu in S} P_mu(s) exp(mu s) on [0, infinity) for nonzero polynomials P_mu in C[X] at distinct rates mu in S with sum_{mu in S} ((d - 1) deg P_mu + 1) = R; (3) over R, srank_R(x |-> phi(||x||^2)) = C_d(R) := sum_{u=1}^m c_d(lambda_u, P_u) = (d - 1) C_2(R) - (d - 2) m, where each real-rate component (Im(lambda_u) = 0) costs c_d = (d - 1) deg P_u + 1 real d-way products (via real Lagrange interpolation) and each nonreal conjugate-pair component (Im(lambda_u) > 0) costs c_d = 2(d - 1) deg P_u + d real d-way products (achieved via an alternating root-of-unity polynomial-product identity giving d rather than 2^{d-1} real products for a complex Gaussian when deg P_u = 0, and proved optimal by Alder-Strassen degree peeling over R); and (4) in d = 2, scalar extension R -> C preserves rank unconditionally and srank_R equals the degree of the minimal monic half-line differential annihilator p(D) phi_C = 0, whereas for every d >= 3 each nonreal conjugate pair incurs a degree-independent real-over-complex rank penalty of d - 2, and every representation R is the uniform limit on compact sets of multi-Gaussian kernels of real rank at most B_d(R) = C_d(R) - (d - 2) sum_u deg P_u (strictly below exact rank whenever d >= 3 and sum_u deg P_u >= 1). Necessity rests on the continuous one-parameter semigroup theorem M(t) = exp(t A) on [0, infinity), for which an observational case study across five proofs (a 96-line Banach-algebra integral-smoothing proof in Lean 4, a 256-line finite-difference proof, and three finite-dimensional nonstandard proofs of 206 and 399 lines in Lean 4 and 275 lines in Isabelle/HOL) illustrates how Mathlib's Bochner-integral library keeps standard integration shorter and valid in infinite dimensions even after homogeneous scaling eta = eps + ||M(eps) - 1|| eliminates the 124-line difference-quotient bound. Finally, we connect the root-of-unity identity to planar harmonic ("beach-ball") differential operators, evaluate reproducible illustrative GPU and CPU case studies (with explicit coefficients in Appendix A) for 2-D circular lens blur (a four-stage separableChannels conditioning ablation for IEEE float16 sRGB rendering across 20 HDR scenes, plus visual and quantitative comparisons against direct discrete rank-R optimization) and 3-D homogeneous-room acoustic leapfrog stencils (R = 1--9, compared against 7-point, 13-point O(dx^4, dt^2), 27-point IWB, fourth-order 25-point O(dx^4, dt^4), and periodic cuFFT k-space baselines), and document practical trade-offs, hardware sensitivity, wide-stencil boundary obstacles, and open questions. All Lean 4 and Isabelle/HOL proof sources, Python/PyTorch/Triton optimization and benchmark scripts, JSON numerical archives, and figure/paper build scripts are publicly available under CC0 1.0 at https://github.com/OlliNiemitalo/kernel-rank-lean.
